paragraphs: Tzarik lizzaher beribbit vekamma lavyan neemru bo shehammalveh ober beshishsha lavyan:

clarification.explanation: One must be very careful with the prohibition of interest (ribbit). The Torah forbade it in many prohibitions, and one who lends with interest transgresses six separate negative commandments.
takeaways: One must be very careful not to lend with interest, since the lender transgresses six negative commandments.

paragraphs: Vhlvh vbr bshlshh lvyn

clarification.explanation: Following the fact that the lender transgresses six negative commandments regarding interest, the borrower himself — one who takes a loan on condition of interest — also transgresses three Torah-level negative commandments, even though he is the party in need of the money and suffering from the transaction.
takeaways: A borrower who takes an interest loan transgresses three Torah-level prohibitions, in addition to the lender's six.

paragraphs: Veheareb vehaedim vehassoper oberim bishne lavyan:

clarification.explanation: Continuing the list of those who transgress the interest prohibitions: the guarantor for the debt (one who guarantees on the borrower's behalf), the witnesses who sign the interest-bearing loan document, and the scribe who writes the interest loan document — each of them transgresses two Torah-level prohibitions.
takeaways: The guarantor, the witnesses, and the scribe each transgress two Torah-level prohibitions, regarding an interest-bearing loan.

paragraphs: Vehassarsur vekol hamsayyea baddabar o hammoreh maqom lilvat o lehalvot oberim belav delipne ivver veku':

clarification.explanation: The broker (intermediary) and anyone who assists in an interest loan transaction, or even one who merely shows another person where to borrow or lend with interest — all of them transgress the prohibition "you shall not place a stumbling block before the blind," since they are assisting a transgression.
takeaways: It is forbidden to assist an interest loan in any way — whether by brokering, practical help, or directing someone to a place that lends with interest.

paragraphs: "p sheim lo yilveh hammalveh hazzeh leloveh zeh, yelek halloveh hazzeh veyilveh miyyisrael acher apillu hake ober hammalveh belipne ivver vehalloveh gam ken ober, "p deim lo haya loveh hu mizzeh hayisrael haya lava mimmennu yisrael acher abal heareb vehaedim vehassoper enam oberim belipne ivver ella davqa beani sheillule hem lo haya zeh hammalveh malveh lazeh, abal im gam baladam haya malveh oto enam oberim belipne ivver veraq oberim al lo tesimun alayv neshek v"g deen oberim belav delipne ivver hare hem machaziqim yede obere abera deyesh bazeh issura derabbanan vehassarsur vekol mi shemmesayyea baddabar en beyadam ella issur derabbanan demachziqin beyad obere abera:

clarification.explanation: Even if the borrower could obtain an interest loan from another Jew, the lender still transgresses "before the blind" (the prohibition of causing a person to stumble in a transgression), and the borrower himself also transgresses it. Regarding the guarantor, witnesses, and scribe — they transgress "before the blind" only in a case involving a poor borrower, where without their involvement the lender would not have lent to him. But if the lender would have lent to the borrower even without them, they do not transgress "before the blind," but only the prohibition "you shall not place interest upon him." Although they carry no Torah-level "before the blind" prohibition, they carry a rabbinic prohibition of strengthening the hands of transgressors. The broker and anyone assisting such a transaction likewise carry only the rabbinic prohibition of strengthening the hands of transgressors.
takeaways: The lender and borrower transgress "before the blind" even if the borrower could obtain an interest loan elsewhere.
The guarantor, witnesses, and scribe transgress "before the blind" only with a poor borrower whose loan depends on them; otherwise they carry another Torah prohibition plus a rabbinic one.
The broker and any assistant carry only the rabbinic prohibition of strengthening the hands of transgressors.

paragraphs: Gam beribbit derabbanan ramu rabbanan al hammalveh kol issure lavyan hannizkar leel abal al halloveh la ramu rabbanan ella raq issur lav delipne ivver veyesh omerim degam haedim en oberim beribbit derabbanan ella raq al issur delipne ivver veayyen chavvat daat bechiddushim:

clarification.explanation: Even with rabbinically forbidden interest (a lighter prohibition than Torah-level interest), the Sages imposed on the lender all the aforementioned negative-commandment-type prohibitions. But on the borrower, the Sages did not impose many negative prohibitions, only one: "before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block." And there are views that even the witnesses (who sign the loan) do not transgress negative prohibitions regarding rabbinic interest, only the "before the blind" prohibition. One should examine the book "Chavot Da'at" in its novellae for further clarification.
takeaways: With rabbinic-level interest, the lender transgresses all the negative prohibitions, while the borrower transgresses only "before the blind."
Some hold the witnesses too transgress only "before the blind" — further clarification is found in "Chavot Da'at."

paragraphs: Min hattora muttar lehalvot lenakeri beribbit velilvat mehem diktib lenakeri tashshik ubizman hattannaim aseru chaza"l lehalvot lahem kede shello yilmod mimmaasehem velo hittiru ella kede chayyayv veaach"k chazeru hachakamim za"l vehittiru halvaa lenakeri beribbit legamre apillu yoter mikkede chayyayv kedin shel tora vekol yisrael shemmalveh meotayv leyisrael beribbit vetoleh otam banuy sheomer shel goy hem hqb"h yipra mimmennu:

clarification.explanation: By Torah law it is permitted to lend to a gentile with interest and also to borrow from him with interest, as it is written, "to a foreigner you may lend with interest." In the era of the Tannaim, the Sages forbade lending to a gentile with interest, so a Jew would not learn from their bad deeds, and permitted it only when needed for his livelihood. Later the Sages reverted and permitted lending to a gentile with interest entirely, even more than needed for his livelihood, as by Torah law. And any Jew who lends his own money to another Jew with interest, but claims the money is not his but belongs to a gentile (as though he is merely the gentile's agent, so the interest would appear permitted) — the Holy One will exact punishment from him.
takeaways: It is permitted to lend to and borrow from a gentile with interest, without limitation.
It is forbidden to lend your own money to a Jew with interest while falsely claiming the money belongs to a gentile, to disguise it as the gentile's agency and thereby permit the interest.

paragraphs: Mumar sheyyatza min hakkelal muttar lehalvot lo beribbit abal asur lilvot mimmennu beribbit mihu im zeh hammumar hu niknas bedat yishmael shemmodin beyichud veen lahem shittup az gam lehalvot lo beribbit asur veken haqqaraim asur lehalvotam beribbit vekol shekken deasur lilvat mehem:

clarification.explanation: A Jew who converted to another religion and left the community of Israel — it is permitted to lend him money with interest, but forbidden to take an interest loan from him. However, if this apostate joined the Islamic faith, which believes in God's unity with no association, then even lending him with interest is forbidden. Likewise, it is forbidden to lend Karaites with interest, and all the more so it is forbidden to take an interest loan from them.
takeaways: For an ordinary apostate, it is permitted to lend with interest, but forbidden to borrow from him with interest.
For an apostate who became Muslim, or for a Karaite, it is forbidden even to lend with interest, and certainly forbidden to borrow from them.

paragraphs: Min hattora en haribbit asur ella derek halvaa verabbotenu za"l asu harchaqa mishmeret laddabar veameru kelala deribbita kol shehu agar natar asur perush kol shemmarvicha bishbil hamtanat meotayv asur ben shebba lo hachob bederek halvaa ben bederek miqqach umimkar ben derek sekirut ben derek melaka ben ribbit muqdemet shemmaqdim haribbit qodem hahalvaa ben ribbit meucheret dilachar shehechezir lo maot shehilva lo noten lo ribbit v"p shello qatzatz immo bishat halvaa kelum ella achar shezzeh taba mimmennu hammaot shennosheh bo natan lo ribbit kede sheyyarchib lo hazzeman vaapillu shechob zeh lo haya iqqaro halvaa ella shel miqqach umimkar vekayyotze bekol zeh aseru rabbotenu za"l haribbit:

clarification.explanation: By Torah law, the interest prohibition applies only to a loan. But our Sages extended the prohibition and stated a rule: any profit arising from the waiting period on money is forbidden. That is, any situation where a person profits merely because he is waiting on his money is forbidden — whether the debt arose from a loan, from a purchase and sale, from rental, or from labor, and whether the interest was given in advance before the loan, or after the borrower already returned the principal. Even if interest was not agreed upon at the time of the loan, but the borrower gave an addition only after the lender demanded the debt, in order to receive more time — this too is forbidden. And all this is true even when the original debt was not a loan but a debt arising from a purchase and sale and the like.
takeaways: Any profit arising from waiting on money is rabbinically forbidden, not only in a direct loan.

The prohibition applies to advance interest, deferred interest, or interest given after a debt demand to gain time, even without prior agreement, and even when the debt arose from a non-loan transaction.

paragraphs: Apillu im malveh reuben maot leshimon veeno qotzetz immo haribbit ella malvehu beinyan sheim yarvicha yitten lo rivvach veim yapsid yihyeh hahepsed kullo al halloveh venimtza shehammalveh qarob lesakar verachoq mehepsed gam bazeh aseru chaza"l:

clarification.explanation: Even in a case where Reuven lends money to Shimon without fixing a set interest rate between them, but they agree that if Shimon profits from the money he will give Reuven a share of the profit, but if there is a loss — the entire loss falls on Shimon alone (so the lender benefits from the profit but does not share in the loss), even in such a case our Sages forbade the transaction.
takeaways: It is forbidden to structure a loan transaction where the lender shares in the profits but not the losses.
This prohibition applies even when no fixed interest rate was set in advance.

paragraphs: Lo yomar reuben leshimon halveni hayyom veaach"k gam ani elohha leka vaapillu im reuben lava mishshimon setam vela amar lo kelum veaach"k chozer reuben umalveh leshimon veomer lo ani malveh leka bishbil shehilvitani miqqodem asur ella yalvu zeh mizzeh bistam been omer veen debarim:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for Reuven to say to Shimon, "lend me today and afterward I too will lend you." And even if Reuven borrowed from Shimon plainly with no condition at all, and afterward Reuven lends to Shimon and says "I am lending you because you lent me earlier" — this is forbidden. Rather, they should lend to each other plainly, without such statements and conditions.
takeaways: It is forbidden to lend on condition of a reciprocal loan.
It is forbidden to present a loan as compensation for a prior loan — one should lend plainly.

paragraphs: Lava bistam uperao veaach"k shegger lo halloveh doron bishbil shehilvahu zo ribbit meucheret vaasura midderabbanan mihu dabar muat share kevan deeno meparesh sheshsholeach lo bishbil shehilvahu veyesh mattirin apillu bedabar merubbeh im sholeach lo haddoron achar sheaberu yamim harbeh meet happeraon veyesh mattirin beopen zeh "p shehalloveh mitkavven belibbo lishloach haddoron bishbil hahalvaa shehilvahu im kol zeh kevan sheaberu yamim harbeh achar happeraon veeno meparesh bepiv kelum muttar veayyen beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman seip z' veayyen chakemat adam ushear acharonim:

clarification.explanation: One who borrowed plainly and repaid his debt, and afterward sent the lender a gift because he had lent him money — this is "deferred interest," rabbinically forbidden. But a small item is permitted, since it is not stated explicitly that it is given for the loan. Some permit even a large item if sent long after repayment, and some permit it even if he intends in his heart that it is for the loan, as long as much time has passed and he does not state this verbally.
takeaways: A thank-you gift after repayment is "deferred interest," rabbinically forbidden.
A small item is permitted; a large item only long after repayment and without stating it explicitly.

paragraphs: Im beet happeraon shehu porea lo mosip lo yoter min sak shehilvahu apillu mosip lo dabar muat vaapillu sheeno meparesh kelum asur middibre soperim bammeh debarim amurim? keshehu chayyab lo maot betorat halvaa uba atta liproa lo maot shehilvahu abal im reuben natan leshimon al sechora kegon shennatan lo maot kede latet lo chittin vekayyotze keneged hammaot veatta keshebba shimon liproa liruben hachittin hosip lo chittin yoter mikkeneged meotayv muttar deamerinan ozeli qa mezal gabbeh kelomar moker lo hassechora yor bezol mimmah shehitna immo umihu im mosip lo harbeh shennikkar bevadday shemmosip lo bishbil shehimtin lo bepiron hassechora "p shehu qibbel hammaot betorat meker, hare zeh chashib kimparesh veasur leqabbel mimmennu hattosepet shehosip lo veayyen beshulchan aruk lerabbenu zalman seip ch':

clarification.explanation: If at the time of repayment the borrower adds more than the amount borrowed — even a small addition and even without stating it explicitly — it is forbidden by the words of the scribes, when this concerns a loan debt. But if Reuven gave Shimon money for merchandise (for example, paid in advance for wheat), and when Shimon delivers the wheat he adds more — this is permitted, since it is said the seller is giving him a discount. Nevertheless, if he adds a great deal, in a manner clearly for the waiting period, it is considered explicit and forbidden.
takeaways: Any addition upon repaying a loan is forbidden.
An addition of merchandise in a transaction paid for in advance is permitted (as a discount), unless the addition is large and clearly for the waiting period.

paragraphs: Im makar reuben sechora leshimon behaqqapa al zeman yadua veabar zeman happeraon shello para lo bizmanno veaach"k beet sheppara lo hosip lo yoter "p shennatan bistam sheeno mazkir shennoten bishbil ikkabt hammaot shennitakkebu etzlo asur "p demaot ellu hem deme sechora yaan dehaka lekka lememar ozeli qa mezal gabbeh veod kevan shezzaqap alayv deme hassechora yesh lazeh din milveh veayyen chakemat adam:

clarification.explanation: If Reuven sold merchandise to Shimon on credit (deferred payment) for a known term, and the repayment time passed, and when he repaid he added more — even though given plainly without mentioning it is for the waiting period — it is forbidden. Although this is merchandise money, here one cannot say he is giving a discount, and since the debt was fixed, it has the law of a loan.
takeaways: An addition upon late repayment of a credit sale is forbidden, since the fixed debt has the law of a loan.

paragraphs: Im hilva baal melaka veoseh lammalveh melaka bezol yoter millishar adam kede sheyyarvicha lo hazzeman hare zeh ribbit shel tora veim kebar hirvicha lo hazzeman veeno tobeo veachar zeh oseh lo bezol hare zeh dabeq ribbit veasur midderabbanan:

clarification.explanation: If the borrower is a craftsman and does work for the lender more cheaply than for others, so the lender will extend the loan's time — this is Torah-level interest. And if he already extended the time and is not demanding repayment, and afterward does work for him cheaply — this is "dust of interest," rabbinically forbidden.
takeaways: Discounted work from a borrower in order to extend a loan = Torah-level interest.
Discounted work done after the extension was already granted = rabbinic-level "dust of interest."

paragraphs: Asur lehaqdim sekar melaka leumman kede sheyyaaseh lo bezol, mippene shennireh kimlavveh lo hayyom kede sheyyozil biskaro: kevan shehaumman yakol lachazor bo, min haddin, shello laasot hammelaka lebaal habbayit, vehammaot sheqqibbel mibbaal habbayit hem chob alayv, vahare zeh kehalvaa veasur: abal im beet shemmaqdim lo hassakar hu matchil laasoq beotah melaka, muttar, mippene denikkar haddabar deellu hammaot hem deme hassekirut, velo niret kehalvaa.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to advance payment to a craftsman so he will do the work cheaply, since this appears as a loan to him (lending him today so he lowers his price): since the craftsman can legally back out, the money he received is considered a debt owed by him, and this is like a loan. But if, at the time the payment is advanced, the craftsman immediately begins working on that job, it is permitted, since then it is clear the money is wage payment, not a loan.
takeaways: Advancing wages to a craftsman so he lowers his price appears as an interest loan and is forbidden.
It is permitted if the craftsman begins the work immediately upon payment (then it is clearly wages).

paragraphs: Reuben sheyyesh lo chatzer verotzeh lehaskir leshimon leshana o shenatayim muttar lehozil hassekirut kede leqabbel atta deme hassekirut velo od ella muttar name lomar leshimon im titten li hassekirut atta ani maskiro beeser veim leachar zeman ani maskiro leka bishnayim asara yaan ki hassekirut dinah hu deenah mishtallemet ella lebassop nimtza sekum sheyyipra lebassop zehu shaveyah shel sekirut hechatzer ukeshepporea lo akshav eser mozil hu lo bashshebi haqdamatah bammeh debarim amurim? kesheomer lo qodem sheyyiqneh hassekirut beechad middarke hahaqnaot abal im kebar gamar immo erek sekirut hechatzer baasara sheyyipra lo atta bimzumman venatan lo shetar hahaqnaa sheen baal hechatzer yukal lachazor bo velo hassoker veachar shehiqna hassoker kepi haddin beerek haeser omer lo tamtin bead hassekirut leachar zeman vaashallem leka y"b hare zeh asur dezeh hattosepet have ribbit gemura:

clarification.explanation: One who rents out a courtyard for one or two years may lower the rent to receive the money now, and may even say "if you pay now — ten, and if later — twelve." The reason: rent is paid only at the end, so the final sum is the true value, and paying ten now is a discount for advance payment. All this applies as long as the transaction has not been finalized by a formal act of acquisition; but if they already agreed on ten in cash now and signed a binding contract that neither party can retract, and then he says "wait on the payment and pay twelve later" — this is forbidden, since this addition is full interest.
takeaways: Discounting rent for advance payment is permitted, even offering "now for ten / later for twelve" — before the transaction is finalized by acquisition.
After a binding acquisition, an addition for deferring payment is full interest and forbidden.

paragraphs: Im reuben makar sechora leshameo baasara al menat sheyyitten lo haddamim miyyad asur lehosip aach"k al hammiqqach velomar amtin leka ad asara chodashim vetitten li y"b bidme hassechora veribbit gemura hi zo vaapillu qodem shennigmar hammiqqach, asur middibre soperim lomar hammoker: im taqqana bemaot medudim lealtar emkor beeser veim leachar y"b chodashim emkor by"b yaan kevan sheamar im yeshallem lealtar yimkor baasara nimtza deme hassechora hahi asara veim aach"k yiqqachenna by"b bishbil shemmamtin lo y"b chodesh hare zeh ribbit derabbanan:

clarification.explanation: If Reuven sold merchandise to Shimon for ten payable immediately, it is forbidden to add afterward and say "I will wait ten months for you and you will pay twelve" — this is full interest. And even before the sale is finalized, it is rabbinically forbidden to say "if you buy in cash — ten, and if after a year — twelve," since from the moment a cash price of ten was set, that is its true value, and taking twelve for the waiting period is rabbinic interest.
takeaways: "A low cash price versus a higher deferred price" is forbidden as interest from the moment a base cash price is set (even before the sale is finalized).

paragraphs: Kol sechora sheshshumatah yedua shehi nimkeret baasara bemaot medudim asur lemakerah besak yoter behaqqapa mihu bazzeman hazzeh nohagim haolam limkor kol min sechora behaqqapa besak yoter yaan ki "p sheyyesh lah shaar yadua bashshuq beotah hair shehi nimkar beeser bemaot medudim vezeh mokerah by"b behaqqapa en zeh niqra shaar yadua yaan ki epshar shebbezo hashshaa shehu moker shaveh eser by"b behaqqapa, yabo yedia meare eroppa shennitchaddesh ezeh dabar hannogea leoto hammin veala hashshaar sheaz gam beir zo yaaleh hashshaar vetihyeh shaveh y"b bemaot medudim vekol shekken achar shennitchaddesh htylgr"p baolam. velaken nahagu hetter bekol mine sechorot limkor dabar sheshshaveh asar bemiddudim by"b behaqqapa vehassibbot asher yesabbebu aliyyat hashshaar bemine hassechorot hem metzuyim bazzeman hazzeh uqerobim lihyot yoter meoto hattaam shekkatab raabya"h za"l shave mishshum delipamim baim sarim veyachamdu hamilim liqnotam beyoter mishshavevayom ukemo shekkatab b"shilte haggibborim" bepereq ezehu neshek ayyen sham. veken samak al zeh harab mahari"y hallevi za"l kelal va"v siman n" dap q"g " veayyen mah shekkatab harab hakkeneset haggedola za"l siman q"g haggahat hattur ot z' yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: Merchandise whose known cash value is ten — by strict law it is forbidden to sell it on credit for more. But in our time the custom is to sell all merchandise on credit for more, since even though there is a known cash market price, selling on credit for twelve is not considered a "fixed price" — the price might rise (news from Europe, the telegraph, officials wanting to buy at a high price, etc.), in which case it would be worth twelve even in cash. Therefore the custom permits selling something worth ten in cash for twelve on credit.
takeaways: Selling on credit above the known cash price is forbidden by strict law, but the custom permits it, since the possibility of a price rise means the credit price is not a fixed addition purely for time.

paragraphs: Im makar sechora by"b behaqqapa lizman y"b chodashim venigmar hammiqqach bazeh uqenao halloqeach venaasa shello az muttar limkor lomar lalloqeach im retzoneka ten li atta maot medudim veennakeh leka asara lemea o y"b lemea min hammiqqach veim halloqeach lo ratza bekak ella amar ani ashallem y"b bizman happeraon kaasher qaniti en bekak kelum umuttar lammoker leqabbel mimmennu y"b bizman happeraon "p sheamar lo shehu merutztzeh leqabbel pachot my"b im yitten lo maot medudim mippene sheellu haddebarim amar hammoker achar shennigmar hammiqqach venaasu hy"b chob al halloqeach:

clarification.explanation: If merchandise was sold for twelve on a year's credit, and the sale was finalized and the buyer acquired it — then the seller may say to the buyer, "if you wish, give me cash now and I will deduct ten or twelve percent for you." And if the buyer refuses and says, "I will pay twelve at the time as I bought it," there is nothing wrong with this, and the seller may accept twelve at repayment time, even though he offered less for cash, since these words were said after the sale was finalized and the twelve became a fixed debt on the buyer.
takeaways: After a credit sale is finalized (and the higher price is already a fixed debt), it is permitted to offer a discount for early cash payment — and if the buyer refuses, to collect the full price.

paragraphs: Yesh matnim bitchillat hammiqqach shemmokerim behaqqapa lekamma chodashim shekkol zeman sheyyihyeh lalloqeach maot yebiem lammoker vinakkeh lo min haddamim echad lemea bead kol chodesh hare zeh asur dehave lah kimparesh im meakshav hare hu leka beeser selaim veim laggoren by"b deqayma lan deasur, ken katab mahara"sh abbuhab za"l beseper hazzikronot vehebio hakkeneset haggedola siman qm"g haggahat hattur ot t"v yeuyyan sham: vehinneh ki ken im hammoker makar sechora by"b lizman y"b chodashim vehattenay haya benehem gemar hammiqqach demeatta umeakshav kol zeman sheyyabi halloqeach hammaot yenakkeh lo hammoker min haddamim echad lemea bead kol chodesh vezeh halloqeach lo hebi hammaot qodem hazzeman kelal ella hebiam achar shennishlam zeman y"b chodesh hinneh shurat hadday notenet ledaat harab mahara"sh abbuhab za"l hannizkar leel, shetztzarik hammeker lenakkot middeme hammiqqach y"b lemea yaan ki kepi hattenay hannizkar im haya halloqeach mebi haddamim lealtar haya menakkeh lo y"b lemea venimtza hammoker gilla dato shehu merutztzeh limkor hassechora hahi bemaot medudim bechesron y"b lemea min hassak shemmeqabbel atta veek yeqabbel atta sak al zeh shennimtza meqabbel hayyitron bishbil hazzeman?

clarification.explanation: Some stipulate at the start of a credit sale that whenever the buyer has money, he will bring it and the seller will deduct one percent per month — this is forbidden, since it is effectively stating "now for ten, and later for twelve," which is forbidden. And if he sold for twelve for a year under such a condition from the start, and the buyer did not bring the money early but only at the year's end — by strict law (per Maharshach Avuhav) the seller must deduct twelve percent, since according to the condition, had he paid immediately he would have deducted it, showing he revealed his willingness to sell for less, and he cannot now collect the addition for the waiting time.
takeaways: A prior condition of "monthly deduction for early payment" is forbidden as interest.
If so conditioned, the seller must deduct the full implied discount and not profit from the waiting.

paragraphs: Im makar by"b lizman y"b chodashim vehitna im halloqeach shemmechuyyab lehabi hammaot achar shene chodashim veaz hu yenakkeh lo middeme hammiqqach asara lemea hinneh bevadday im halloqeach hebi hammaot kepi hattenay e bazeh chashash yaan ki bazeh hattenay sheasa hammoker nitbarer shehu merutztzeh limkor sechora zeh pachot asara lemea min haerek shehaya benehem vekak hu qibbel beemet et deme hammiqqach pachot asara lemea: beram mah sheyyesh likora leesor beopen zeh hu beheka dehalloqeach lo hebi deme hammiqqach achar shene chodashim ella nishar etzlo ad sop y"b chodesh delikora nireh deasur lammoker leqabbel mimmennu y"b ella tzarik lenakkot lo asara lemea middeme hammiqqach mihu raiti lehaggaon mhrshd"m za"l beyoreh dea siman s"t, shehebi niddon kazeh veheela meachar shennaasa haddabar "y tenay vehaya epshar leqayyemo velo qiyyemu im ken nitbattel hammiqqach venimtza shellebassop qoneh halloqeach et hammiqqach mechadash veaz hammoker yukal liqqach mimmennu y"b dehave kemoker bemaot medudim by"b yeuyyan sham tamo venimmoqu immo venireh sheggam mahara"sh gaon za"l bemishpatim yesharim siman s"t hiskim immo beiqqar haddin umah shettamah alayv umah sheratza leyashsheb debarayv hairoti alayv bsh"q mqbtzyl vesham himlatzti bead hmhrshd"m za"l beopen acher veek sheyyihyeh baiqqar yesh lismok al mhrshd"m za"l lehattir bazeh veal oto open sheasarnu bisip haqqodem hinneh sham bsh"q mqbtzyl asiti taqqana shene opannim lehattir haddabar:

clarification.explanation: If sold for twelve for a year, with a condition that the buyer must bring the money after two months and then receive a ten-percent deduction — if the buyer brought it according to the condition, there is no concern, since the seller revealed he is willing to sell for less. The question is when the buyer did not bring it after two months but left it until the year's end: seemingly it would be forbidden to accept twelve (requiring a ten-percent deduction). However, the Maharshdam ruled: since this was done under a condition that could have been fulfilled and was not, the sale is voided, and it follows that the buyer is buying anew at the end, at which point it is permitted to collect twelve (as a cash sale at twelve). Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes that in his book Miqabtzeel he established two ways to permit this.
takeaways: A discount condition for early payment is valid if fulfilled; if not fulfilled, according to the Maharshdam the sale is voided and the buyer buys anew, permitting collection of the full price.

paragraphs: Reuben yesh lo chob al shimon mea denerim lizman shelosha chodashim muttar lomar leshimon tipchot min hachob shelosha denerim vetitten li tishim vesheba denerim hayyom vehippater! veen bazeh shum issur kelal:

clarification.explanation: Reuven has a debt owed by Shimon of one hundred dinars for a term of three months — it is permitted to say to Shimon, "reduce it by three dinars and give me ninety-seven today and you are released." There is no prohibition in this at all.
takeaways: A creditor may offer the debtor a discount in exchange for early repayment of the debt — entirely permitted.

paragraphs: Reuben sheyyesh lo milva al peh lizman al shimon muttar limkor hachob lelevi bepachot kede sheyyeqabbel hammaot millevi ak tzarik lizkot levi bechob zeh bemaamad shelashettan deen chob b"p niqneh ella bemaamad shelashettan sheyyomar reuben leshimon bipne levi ten lelevi chob peloni sheyyesh li etzleka veim lo tiqnehu bemaamad shelashettan lo qana levi veaz hammaot shennatan levi liruben hem chashibi halvaa vela deme meker hem ulehaki, harvachat happechat shellevi noten tishim vesheba veloqeach mea have ribbit veasur: bammeh debarim amurim? bechob sheyyesh leyisrael al yisrael abal im hachob sheyyesh leyisrael al hannakeri eno niqneh bemaamad shelashettan ketzad yaaseh yomar haqqoneh lammoker atta timchol lenakeri vetipterehu mikkol vakol bead maot ellu sheani noten leka ubemaot ellu ani qoneh mimmeka kol mah sheani yakol lehotzi min hannakeri veaz "g deen hachob hazzeh asher al nakeri niqneh leyisrael mikkol maqom hare nistalleq mimmennu yisrael hammoker betorat mechila veen yisrael haqqoneh notel kelum mishshel yisrael hammoker ubilbad shello yihyeh yisrael hammoker areb lehaqqoneh apillu bead haqqeren lebaddo ella tihyeh kol achrayut hachob al haqqoneh veen al hammoker kelum vekannizkar beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman seip s"t yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: Reuven, who has an oral loan (without a document) owed by Shimon, may sell the debt to Levi for less to receive cash, but he must transfer it to Levi in the presence of all three: Reuven says to Shimon, in Levi's presence, "give Levi the debt you owe me." Without the presence of all three, Levi has not acquired it, and the money he gave is considered a loan rather than a purchase price, in which case the profit from the discount (giving ninety-seven and taking one hundred) is interest and forbidden. All this concerns a debt of a Jew owed by a Jew; but a debt owed by a gentile is not acquired through the presence of all three — its remedy is that the buyer says to the seller, "forgive the gentile and release him in exchange for the money I am giving, and with it I am buying whatever I can collect from the gentile," provided the seller bears no guarantee whatsoever to the buyer and all responsibility falls on the buyer.
takeaways: Selling an oral loan for less requires the "presence of all three"; otherwise it is an interest loan and forbidden.
A debt owed by a gentile — through a mechanism of forgiveness, with all responsibility on the buyer.

paragraphs: Yisrael sheyyesh lo shetar chob al yisrael chabero bemea dinarim lizman shene chodashim o yoter verotzeh lemakero yisrael acher bepachot kede leqabbel hammaot miyyad tzarik sheyyimkerennu lo biktiba umesarah dehaynu sheyyiktob al gup hashshetar o bishtar acher ek makarti liploni ben peloni shetar chob zeh ihu vekol shibuda deit beh ketaqqanat chaza"l umasarti lo hashshetar veamarti lo qane lak hay shetara vekol shibuda deit beh veken yaaseheh mammash sheyyimsor lo hashshetar vayyomer lo qane lak hay shetara vekol shibuda deit beh veal yede kak niqneh hachob shebbashshetar leyisrael haqqoneh umuttar lo leharvicha happechat sheppochet min hachob vekol zeh bishtar sheyyesh leyisrael al yisrael abal shetar chob sheyyesh leyisrael al haggoy i epshar lemakero bederek zeh sheen hachob asher al hannakeri niqneh beshum qinyan vetaqqanato laasot beopen shekkatabnu bisip qodem:

clarification.explanation: A Jew who has a promissory note against his fellow Jew for one hundred dinars for a term of two months or more, and wishes to sell it to another Jew for less to receive cash immediately, must sell it by "writing and delivery": he writes on the note itself (or on another document) that he sold the note and all its liens to so-and-so, as instituted by the Sages, and delivers the note to him saying, "acquire this note and every lien in it." This transfers the debt to the buyer and he may profit from the discount. All this concerns a note of a Jew against a Jew; but a note against a gentile cannot be sold this way (a debt against a gentile is not acquired by any act of acquisition), and its remedy is as in the previous paragraph.
takeaways: Selling a Jew's promissory note against a Jew for less requires writing and delivery.
A note against a gentile — through the forgiveness method in the previous paragraph.

paragraphs: "g deen hashshetar niqneh ella biktiba umesira kaamur leel mikkol maqom bazzeman hazzeh shetar sheqqorin kmbyyl"h (shetar lmvk"z, lipquddat matztzig hashshetar) shekkatub bo ani mechuyyab lemor bipne peloni sak kak vekak veyiktob bo hazzeman vegam yiktob bo shem hair shehu koteb vechotem bah vegam yiktob shehassak hazzeh higgia leyado bemiddudim o becheshbon o deme sechora hinneh lishtar zeh qorin oto kmbyyl"h. vekevan denaasa baopen hannizkar sheamarnu az zeh nimkar bedina demalkuta keminhag hassocharim mizzeh lazeh "y ketiba zo sheqqeruyan giro (hassibba) dehaynu shezzeh reuben asher shimon nitchayyeb lo bashshetar kesak hakkatub bo yiktob hu al gup hashshetar nosach zeh vnn" tdp" lm"r (=na leshallem lipquddat) yehuda ben yaaqob sak hakkatub bishtar zeh uketiba zo qorin otah giro vetaspiq bedina demalkuta keminhag hassocharim sheyyihyeh niqneh shetar hkmbyyl"h hazzeh meechad leechad al derek zo umeachar deqayma lan beinyanim kaelleh dina demalkuta dina laken gam bedinenu niqneh shetar hkmbyyl"h bederek zeh veen tzarik ketiba umesira umehanne gam leani issur ribbit vekannizkar bapposeqim za"l vekullan gam im yihyeh shetar kmbyyl"h zeh leyisrael al hannakeri yukal lemakero leyisrael bederek ketiba zo hannizkeret leel sheqqorin giro:

clarification.explanation: Although a note is generally acquired only by writing and delivery, in our time a note called a "kambiyala" (a bearer note / order note), containing an obligation to pay a specified sum to so-and-so, with the date, city name, and a statement that the sum was received — is sold according to "the law of the land" and merchant custom by means of an endorsement called "giro": the holder writes on the note, "please pay to the order of so-and-so the sum written in this note," and this writing suffices. And since "the law of the land is law," in our own halacha too a kambiyala note is acquired this way without writing and delivery, and this is also effective regarding the interest prohibition — even for a note of a Jew against a gentile.
takeaways: A modern bill of exchange (kambiyala) transfers by endorsement ("giro") following the law of the land and merchant custom, without writing and delivery.
This method is also effective for the interest permission, even for a note against a gentile.

paragraphs: Ha deamarnu demuttar leyisrael limkor shetar chob sheyyesh lo al chabero biktiba umesira bepachot kede leqabbel hammaot miyyad haynu davqa im tihyeh achrayut hachob al haqqoneh dehaynu sheim heani halloveh veen lo leshallem lo yukal haqqoneh litboa min hammoker kelum abal im achrayut zo al hammoker sheim heani halloveh yitba haqqoneh et hammoker leshallem - asur liqnot bepachot limsor tishim vesheba bead mea. veken hu haddin bishtar zeh shel hqmbyyl"h asher niqneh "y ketiba hannizkeret sheqqorin giro tzarik sheyyeparesh hammoker beperush biktiba zo shel haggiru shehu eno meqabbel alayv achrayut dehaynu shekkatub kak "vaanana tedappea mublag el middekur lemor pilan chvlh qebala keullatz el tobeah min dun ragua" (=na leshallem hassak hannizkar lipquddat peloni, mibbilti achrayut kelal shel shum tebia min hechatum kan) sheim koteb et ha"giro" benussach zeh, az bedina demalkuta keminhag hassocharim patur hammoker min haachrayut umimmela gam bedinenu hu patur umuttar bazeh yaan ki ledaat maran za"l udeimmeh en hetter bimkirat hashshetarot ella im ken yihyeh hammakur patur meachrayut: vehinneh poh irenu bgd"d y" mekirat shetarot ellu sheqqure kmbyyl"h shehem ketubim lizman umokerim otam bepachot kede leqabbel hammaot miyyad metzuvvim harbeh ben yisrael vekol eseq hammischar beir zo taluy bazeh vei epshar baladam ak hem kotebim bistam veen mepareshim bahem al haachrayut ubedina demalkuta beminhag hassocharim im katub higgiru bistam velo peresh al haachrayut yitchayyeb hammoker beachrayut deim lo para hamchuyyab yipra hammoker veqasheh haddabar meod letaqqen sheyyiktob perush bilti achrayut veen anachnu mochin bazeh "p sheanachnu qibbalnu horaat mera"n za"l uledideh tzarik shello yihyeh acharayut al hammoker veamerinan sheyyesh lahem al mah sheyyismoku yaan ki beemet yesh poseqim demattirim apillu im acharayut al hammoker veayyen beseper kepi aharon siman z' sheheerik bedin shetarot hkmbyyl"h hannizkar uberer deikka shalosh chaluqot bazeh yesh poseqim disbira lehu apillu im en hammoker meqabbel alayv ella raq achrayut haqqeren davqa asur veyesh disbira lehu im en meqabbel alayv hammoker ella raq achrayut haqqeren bilbad muttar veheela deken hi sebarat mera"n za"l veyesh disbira lehu apillu im meqabbel hammoker ella raq achrayut haqqeren bilbad muttar veheela deken hi sebarat mera"n za"l veyesh disbira lehu apillu im meqabbel hammoker achrayut haqqeren veharevach name muttar yeuyyan sham hinneh ki ken "g deen anachnu mochin beyad hannohagin hetter "p baale sebarat hammattirim gam bidikka achrayut haqqeren veharevach al hammoker mikkol maqom yere shamayim yizzaher lepachot laasot kisbarat hammattirim bihyot haachrayut al hammoker bead haqqeren bilbad vehammachmir gam bazeh tabo alayv beraka:

clarification.explanation: The leniency to sell a promissory note for less to receive cash immediately applies specifically when the responsibility falls on the buyer — that if the borrower becomes impoverished and does not pay, the buyer has no claim against the seller. But if the responsibility falls on the seller (so the buyer can sue him), it is forbidden to buy for less. Likewise with a kambiyala note acquired by "giro": the seller must specify in writing that he accepts no responsibility; if he wrote so, then according to the law of the land he is exempt from responsibility and it is permitted, since according to Maran the leniency of selling notes applies only when the seller is exempt from responsibility. On this matter, Rabbi Yosef Chaim cites from the book "Kfi Aharon" that there are three approaches among the authorities: some forbid selling for less even when the seller accepts responsibility only for the principal; some permit it when the seller's responsibility is only for the principal — this being Maran's view; and some permit it even when the seller accepts responsibility for both the principal and the profit. In Baghdad such sales are very widespread and all commerce depends on them, but they write plainly without specifying the responsibility, and according to merchant custom, plain writing obligates the seller in responsibility; and it is very difficult to arrange for them to write "without responsibility," and one should not protest against them, since they have authorities among the permitting views to rely upon. And one who fears Heaven should be careful at least to follow the permitting view when the seller's responsibility is for the principal alone and not also the profit, and one who is stringent even about this is blessed.
takeaways: Selling a note/kambiyala for less is permitted only when the seller bears no recourse liability (writing "without responsibility" in the giro).

Among the authorities there are three approaches: forbidding even when responsibility is limited to the principal; permitting when limited to the principal (Maran's view); and permitting even when responsibility covers both principal and profit.

The Baghdad custom of plain writing (which imposes responsibility) relies on the permitting authorities; the God-fearing should minimize the seller's responsibility to the principal alone, and one who is even more stringent is blessed.
